title: Advanced Phrasal Verbs 2
completion_message: ¡Magnífico! Dominar estos Phrasal Verbs avanzados te permite discutir estrategias, conflictos y transiciones corporativas con total naturalidad.

stages.title: Phrasal Verbs de Negocios Nivel B2 (Parte 2)

parts.visual:
Estrategia y Decisiones: 
- Rule out (Descartar una opción/posibilidad). 
Ej: We cannot rule out the possibility of a merger. 
- Phase out (Retirar gradualmente un producto). 
Ej: We will phase out the old software over the next year.
parts.audio: Strategy and Decisions. 'Rule out' means to exclude or eliminate an option. For example: We cannot rule out the possibility of a merger. 'Phase out' means to gradually stop using or producing something. For example: We will phase out the old software over the next year.

parts.visual:
Conflictos y Posiciones: 
- Back down (Echarse atrás / Ceder en una disputa). 
Ej: They threatened to sue us, but they backed down. 
- Step down (Dimitir / Renunciar a un cargo importante). 
Ej: The CEO decided to step down after the scandal.
parts.audio: Conflicts and Positions. 'Back down' means to withdraw from a conflict or give in. For example: They threatened to sue us, but they backed down. 'Step down' means to resign from an important position. For example: The CEO decided to step down after the scandal.

stages.title: Interactive Quiz
stages.description: Elige el Phrasal Verb avanzado correcto para la situación de negocios.

questions.question: The police haven't ____ ____ the possibility of corporate espionage. (Descartado).
questions.explanation: Rule out = descartar, eliminar como posibilidad.

questions.question: Due to health reasons, the Chairman will ____ ____ next month. (Dimitir de un cargo alto).
questions.explanation: Step down = dimitir, renunciar (especialmente de cargos altos).

questions.question: The union demanded a 10% raise, but the company refused to ____ ____. (Ceder / Echarse atrás).
questions.explanation: Back down = ceder, echarse atrás en una discusión o conflicto.

questions.question: We are going to ____ ____ the old models and introduce the new V2. (Retirar gradualmente).
questions.explanation: Phase out = eliminar o retirar progresivamente (un producto, un sistema).

questions.question: We need to ____ ____ a meeting with the investors next week. (Organizar / Configurar).
questions.explanation: Set up = organizar (una reunión), establecer (una empresa), instalar (un equipo).

questions.question: The government is planning to ____ ____ a new tax on tech companies. (Introducir / Implementar).
questions.explanation: Bring in = introducir o implementar (una nueva ley, producto o sistema).

questions.question: If you want to be successful, you have to ____ ____ from the competition. (Destacar).
Before signing, I need to ____ ____ this contract with my lawyer. (Revisar detalladamente / Discutir).
questions.explanation: Talk over = discutir o revisar un tema detalladamente.

questions.question: We didn't expect the costs to ____ ____ so quickly! (Aumentar / Acumularse).
questions.explanation: Add up = acumularse, sumar (especialmente dinero o gastos).

questions.question: I had to ____ ____ a lot of candidates before finding the right one. (Eliminar / Descartar).
questions.explanation: Weed out = eliminar o filtrar lo que no sirve (candidatos, errores).

questions.question: Our profits have started to ____ ____ after a bad quarter. (Estabilizarse).
questions.explanation: Level off = estabilizarse (después de subir o bajar).

questions.question: They tried to ____ me ____ of the deal, but I refused. (Cortar / Dejar fuera).
questions.explanation: Cut out = dejar a alguien fuera de un trato o actividad.

questions.question: The negotiations ____ ____ for hours without reaching an agreement. (Se alargaron / Arrastraron).
questions.explanation: Drag on = alargarse demasiado o de forma tediosa.

questions.question: I need someone to ____ ____ my responsibilities while I am on vacation. (Asumir / Encargarse de).
questions.explanation: Take on = asumir (responsabilidades, trabajo) o contratar personal.

questions.question: The boss asked me to ____ ____ my proposal during the meeting. (Exponer / Presentar claramente).
questions.explanation: Lay out = exponer, explicar o presentar algo con claridad.

questions.question: We must ____ ____ exactly how much this will cost. (Calcular / Descubrir).
questions.explanation: Figure out = averiguar, calcular, resolver mentalmente.

questions.question: The startup was ____ ____ by a much larger corporation. (Comprada en su totalidad).
questions.explanation: Buy out = comprar la totalidad de una empresa o la parte de un socio.

questions.question: We had to ____ ____ to our emergency fund to pay the rent. (Recurrir a / Usar).
questions.explanation: Fall back on = recurrir a algo como plan B (ahorros, una habilidad).

questions.question: The IT department will ____ ____ the new update tonight. (Lanzar / Desplegar).
questions.explanation: Roll out = lanzar, desplegar (un nuevo producto, software o servicio).

questions.question: If we want to finish by Friday, we really need to ____ ____. (Acelerar el ritmo).
questions.explanation: Speed up = acelerar, hacer algo más rápido.

stages.title: Written Expression
stages.description: Escribe la preposición correcta para el Phrasal Verb.

questions.question: We cannot rule ____ that option. (Descartar)
The CEO will step ____. (Dimitir)
They refused to back ____. (Ceder)
We will phase ____ the old product. (Retirar gradualmente)
Let's set ____ a meeting. (Organizar)
You need to stand ____ from the crowd. (Destacar)
We need to figure it ____. (Averiguar/Resolver)
They will roll ____ the update tonight. (Desplegar/Lanzar)
The costs started to add ____. (Acumularse)
Sales began to level ____. (Estabilizarse)
